This text belongs to the genre of "incantations" or "mythological prologues," often found in the *Edubba* (scribal school) tradition. It describes the primordial state of the world, the creation of the gods, and their subsequent distress.

Here is an English translation based on the standard interpretation of these ritualized lines:

1. In those days, back in those days, when heaven and earth were created.
2. In that night, back in that night, when heaven and earth were created.
3. In those years, back in those years, when fates were decreed.
4. When the Anunnaki gods were born.
5. And the "divine powers" (*nam-NIR.P A*) were established.
6. When the gods were distributed throughout heaven and earth.
7. When the gods were brought forth and birthed.
8. When the gods’ rations were bound into their dining halls.
9. The great gods stood by, and the lesser gods were bearing burdens.
10. The gods were dredging the canals and piling up their silt in the *Ḫarali* (mountain).
11. The gods were grinding grain, setting their lives to the word (of the masters).
12. At that time, wide wisdom existed for the great gods.
13. Enki, in the deep *Engur* (abyss), a place that no other god could look into.
14. He lay upon his bed, and in his sleep, he did not rise.
15. The gods were uttering lamentations, saying "What is this sorrow?"
16. To the one who lay in sleep, from his bed he would not rise.
17. Namma, the primeval mother who gave birth to all the great gods.
18. She brought the lamentation of the gods to her son (Enki).
19. (She said): "He who lies in sleep, he who lies in slumber..."
20. "...[he does not] rise..."
21. "Your created gods are drowning in their (heavy) labors."

***

### Notes on the Translation:
*   **Context:** This text is a variant of the framing for the myth *Enki and Ninmaḫ*, which explains the creation of humanity to relieve the lesser gods of the labor of digging canals and maintaining the earth.
*   **The "Labor" Section (Lines 9-11):** This vivid description illustrates the "strike" of the lesser gods. They complain that the work is too hard, which prompts Enki to create "humanity" to serve as sub-workers for the gods.
*   **"Enki in the Abyss":** Enki is depicted as sleeping in the *Engur* (the primeval waters), disconnected from the toil of the other gods, which is why Namma must come to wake him and alert him to the suffering of the lesser deities.
*   **Linguistic Note:** Lines 1-4 are formulaic "incantation-stretching" lines often used to set the temporal stage for a mythological event.
